chunks: He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Bilal al-Muhallabi reported to us, from Ali ibn Abdillah ibn Asad al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Abi Sayf, from Abu Habab, from Rabi'ah and Umarah and others:

That a group of the companions of the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) came to him when the people had dispersed from him and many of them had fled to Mu'awiyah seeking what was in his hands of worldly goods. They said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, give these riches, and prefer these nobles from the Arabs and Quraysh over the mawali and the non-Arabs, and those whose opposition and flight to Mu'awiyah you fear.

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to them: Do you command me to seek victory through injustice? No! By Allah, I will never do so as long as a sun rises and a star appears in the sky. By Allah, even if their wealth were mine, I would treat them equally among them, so how when it is indeed their own wealth?!

He said: Then the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) fell silent for a long time, then he said: Whoever has wealth, let him beware of corruption, for indeed giving wealth in other than its right is squandering and extravagance, and it, even if it were a mention for its owner in this world, yet it loses it before Allah the Mighty

and Majestic, and never has a man placed his wealth wrongfully and with other than its rightful people except that Allah deprives him of their gratitude, and if their affection was for another, for if there remains with him someone who shows affection and gratitude, then it is only flattery and lies, wanting to draw near to him to obtain from him the like of what used to come to him before. And if his fortune slips and he needs their help or recompense, then the worst friend and most blameworthy companion.

And whoever does good deeds with what Allah gave him, let him maintain kinship, and be good in hospitality, and let him free the captive with it, and let him help the debtor and the wayfarer and the poor and the fighters in the path of Allah, and let him be patient upon calamities and hardships, for indeed triumph through these qualities is the noblest of worldly virtues and the attainment of the virtues of the Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about distributing wealth equally?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (a.s.) refuses his companions' request to distribute public wealth unequally to buy loyalty against Mu'awiyah, declaring he will never seek victory through injustice. He then teaches about the proper use of wealth: giving to the needy, maintaining kinship, and practicing hospitality.
